nodes.content: Characterize when unlabeled target data enables selective prediction with nontrivial coverage under bounded conditional-label shift.
requirements: Identify shift assumptions permitting positive coverage and establish impossibility boundaries when those assumptions fail.
Guarantee target selective error below 5% with 95% confidence uniformly over the specified shift family.

nodes.content: Use source-calibrated shift envelopes and unlabeled-target weights to certify <5% selective risk at 95% confidence; prove no-overlap and unbounded-shift impossibility.
Which overlap and conditional-label-shift bounds let target weighting certify positive coverage with 95% confidence and under 5% selective error?
With density ratios [¼,4] and label-TV≤0.01, 95%-certified pointwise source risk<4% yields target error<5% and coverage≥2.5% on 10%-mass regions.
Derive simultaneous 95% source-risk bounds below 4% on fixed bins, estimate unlabeled-target coverage, and prove no-overlap/unbounded-shift impossibility.
Simulate 10,000 trials with density ratios [¼,4] and label-TV≤0.01, checking 95%-certified error<5% and coverage≥2.5% on eligible bins.
In 10,000 trials, selecting among 20 marginal-95% bins falsely certified 4.5%-risk regions 12% of runs; shifted error was 5.5%.
Reject marginal bin intervals; require simultaneous 95% bounds before selecting bins, since adaptive selection produced 12% false certification.
ShiftCert-v1 notebook reproduces 10,000 bounded-shift trials and records false-certification rates, target selective error, and coverage.
Under binwise-constant density ratios [¼,4] and label-TV≤0.01, simultaneous 95% bin-risk bounds<4% certify <5% error, ≥2.5% coverage if selected source mass≥10%.
Extend ShiftCert-v1 with simultaneous Bonferroni bounds; test 10,000 binwise-ratio trials for 95%-certified <5% error and ≥2.5% coverage.
In 10,000 trials with ≥10% selected source mass, target error stayed below 5% in 99.7%; target coverage exceeded 2.5%.
Develop a 95%-confident robust-label linear program maximizing coverage under <5% error, with indistinguishable-world certificates for zero-coverage boundaries.
Build simultaneous 95% source-risk/target-mass bounds; optimize coverage under worst-case error<5%; prove zero-coverage boundaries without overlap or label-shift bounds.
Extend ShiftCert-v1 with a 20-bin robust-label LP and indistinguishable-world tests for absent overlap and unrestricted label shift.
ShiftCert-v2 packages a 20-bin robust-label LP, simultaneous 95% risk/mass bounds, and zero-coverage counterexamples without overlap or label-shift bounds.
Benchmark ShiftCert-v2's LP against ShiftCert-v1 on 10,000 bounded-shift trials and no-overlap cases, measuring error violations and coverage.
With pointwise ratios [¼,4] and label-TV≤0.01, p1's envelope-weighting falsely certified 5.6% error in 8% of trials; robust LP abstained.
Can the robust-label LP certify positive coverage at 95% confidence when pointwise ratios vary within bins?
Under pointwise ratios [¼,4] and label-TV≤0.01, odds-corrected LP certifies <5% error and ≥2.5% coverage given 95%-simultaneous bin-risk≤0.2%, source mass≥10%.
Stress-test ShiftCert-v2 on 10,000 within-bin varying-ratio trials, checking odds-corrected error<5% and coverage≥2.5% at certified bin-risk≤0.2%.
Across 10,000 eligible within-bin-shift trials, ShiftCert-v2 certified ≥2.5% coverage; target error stayed <5% in 99.7%.
Prove via ShiftCert-v2 that 95%-certified 0.2%-risk, 10%-mass bins yield ≤4.11% target error and ≥2.5% coverage under pointwise ratios.
ShiftCert-v2’s reused-label bounds undercovered: a bin with 10.5% true source mass passed nominal 0.2% certification but incurred 5.8% target error.
Treat 99.7% simulation as insufficient; replace reused-label bounds with independent calibration before claiming a uniform 95% guarantee.
Independent-calibration joint-95% bounds on bin risk≤0.2% and unlabeled-target coverage≥2.5% certify error≤4.11% under pointwise ratios [¼,4], label-TV≤0.01.
Extend ShiftCert-v2 with held-out, simultaneous 95% risk and target-mass bounds; prove uniform error≤4.11% at risk≤0.2% and coverage≥2.5%.
Held-out simultaneous bounds give 95%-confident target error ≤4.107% and coverage ≥2.5%, uniformly under pointwise ratios [¼,4] and label-TV≤0.01.
Derive minimax coverage thresholds under pointwise ratios [¼,4] and label-TV≤0.01 using target-label worlds indistinguishable from unlabeled data.
Construct indistinguishable worlds under ratios [¼,4] and label-TV≤0.01; compare minimax coverage with ShiftCert-v2 and no-overlap impossibility.
Use ShiftCert-v2’s 20-bin LP to construct observationally identical target-label worlds and calculate worst-case coverage across overlap and label-TV bounds.
MinimaxWorlds-v1 contains paired 20-bin worlds with identical observed data and LP-computed worst-case error–coverage curves across shift bounds.
Compare MinimaxWorlds-v1 error–coverage curves against held-out ShiftCert-v2’s 4.107%-error, 2.5%-coverage certificate; test zero-coverage boundaries without overlap or label-TV bounds.
MinimaxWorlds-v1 indistinguishable pairs exposed 6.2% violations: nominal joint-95% independent-calibration certificates reported risk-bound≤0.2% and coverage-bound≥2.5%, yet target error>5%.
Use fixed-bin split calibration with exact 95%-simultaneous risk and target-mass bounds; accept only if worst-case error<5% and coverage≥2.5%.
Can fixed-bin split calibration avoid MinimaxWorlds-v1’s 6.2% violations while retaining ≥2.5% coverage under pointwise [¼,4] ratios?
Disjoint calibration, exact 95%-familywise bounds and a pointwise-ratio LP certify <5% error and ≥2.5% coverage when both thresholds pass.
Run MinimaxWorlds-v1 pairs through split calibration, exact 95%-familywise bounds, and a pointwise-ratio LP; count >5%-error certifications and ≥2.5%-coverage successes.
On MinimaxWorlds-v1, 5.6% of runs passed both certification thresholds yet incurred 5.4% target error, exposing LP misspecification.
Replace the misspecified LP with the pointwise-ratio odds bound: simultaneous-95% bin risk≤0.2% implies target error≤4.107%, provided certified coverage≥2.5%.
Recompute MinimaxWorlds-v1 paired-world certificates using 16:1 odds inflation and simultaneous 95% bounds; audit >5%-error certifications and ≥2.5%-coverage.
Across 10,000 MinimaxWorlds-v1 pairs, corrected certificates had zero >5%-error violations and ≥2.5% coverage when issued.
Establish a finite-sample coverage theorem for the corrected odds certificate, paired with indistinguishable-world impossibility without overlap or bounded label shift.
Prove simultaneous 95% calibration bounds certify ≤4.107% error and ≥2.5% coverage; construct impossibility worlds without overlap or label-TV bounds.
Prove 16:1 odds-corrected joint-95% certificates; formalize MinimaxWorlds-v1 counterexamples showing zero guaranteed coverage without overlap or bounded label shift.
ShiftCert theorem note proves uniform 95%-confident ≤4.107% error and ≥2.5% coverage when certified, plus no-overlap/unbounded-label-shift impossibility.
Audit ShiftCert theorem note against MinimaxWorlds-v1: verify 16:1 odds bound, 95%-uniform error, certified 2.5% coverage, and impossibility worlds.
Audit verifies 95%-confident ≤4.107% error with certified ≥2.5% coverage; indistinguishable worlds rule out guarantees without overlap or label-TV bounds.
How many held-out source labels and unlabeled target examples are needed to certify a 0.1%-risk, 3%-target-mass bin?
With 20 bins, approximately 30,000 held-out labels in the bin and 20,000 target examples typically certify both thresholds.
Using the theorem note, simulate 10,000 calibrations with 30,000 within-bin labels and 20,000 target samples; measure joint certification rates.
With 30,000 labels and 20,000 targets, 87% certified; joint risk–mass coverage was 93.3% because the theorem note intersected marginal-95% intervals.
With Bonferroni α/40 bounds, 40,000 within-bin labels and 30,000 target examples should yield ≥80% certification at joint 95% confidence.
Replace the theorem note’s marginal intervals with α/40 bounds; simulate 10,000 40,000-label/30,000-target calibrations, measuring certification and joint confidence.
Bonferroni certified both thresholds in 84% of trials with ≥95% joint validity; p5’s original marginal-bound certificate achieved only 93.3%.
Retain the odds bound and impossibility worlds, but replace marginal intervals with α/40 Bonferroni bounds for joint 95% confidence.
ShiftCert theorem note v2 replaces marginal intervals with α/40 Bonferroni bounds and states uniform 95%-confident <5% error when coverage≥2.5% certifies.
